255.subject: Botany
255.text: The cells of the quiescent centre are characterised by
options: having dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei
having light cytoplasm and small nuclei
dividing regularly to add to the corpus
dividing regularly to add to tunica
255.sol: In the apices of some roots, (e.g., Zea mays, maize), there is a central region of cells which normally does not divide. This central inactive region was called quiescent centre by F.A.L. Clowes $(1959,1961)$. The cells of this region have lesser amounts of RNA and DNA so they have small nuclei. These cells also have a lower rate of protein synthesis. Mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum are less developed. The cells of the quiescent centre are usually inactive. However, if already existing meristematic cells are injured or become inactive due to any other reason, the cells of quiescent centre become active.

330.text:
Assertion : Algae and fungi are classified as thallophytes.
Reason : They both are autotrophs.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
330.sol: According to Eichler's classification, plant kingdom is divided into two subdivisions cryptogamae and phanerogamae. Cryptogamae has 3 divisions thallophyta, bryophyta and pteridophyta. Thallophyta in turn is divided into 2 classes, algae and fungi. As both these groups have generally undifferentiated plant body (not differentiated into true root, stem and leaves) they are called thallophyta. Also they are non vascular plants. But algae are chlorophyllous and hence show autotrophic mode of nutrition ie can prepare their own food. But fungi are nonchlorophyllous and cannot prepare their own food. So they are heterotrophic in nature.

982.subject: Chemistry
982.text:
Assertion : Increasing pressure on pure water decreases its freezing point.
Reason : Density of water is minimum at $273 \mathrm{~K}$.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true and the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
982.sol:
According to Clapeyron-Clausius equation, $\frac{d T}{d P}=\frac{T\left(V_l-V_s\right)}{\Delta H_f}$
Since density of ice is less than that of water, $V_s$ is greater than $V_l$. In other words, the expression on the right hand side of the above equation is negative. This means that the increase of pressure must lower and decrease of pressure must raise the freezing point.
982.meta: Assertion : Increasing pressure on pure water decreases its freezing point. Reason : Density of water is minimum at 273 ~K .

5793.subject: Chemistry
5793.text:
Assertion (A) Adsorption is an exothermic process.
Reason (R) Physisorption of a gas on a solid surface is normally reversible.
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are correct and $R$ is the correct. explanation of $\mathrm{A}$.
Both $A$ and $R$ are correct but $R$ is not the correct explanation of $\mathrm{A}$.
5793.sol:
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion. The correct reason for given assertion is as follows : When a gas is adsorbed on a solid surface, its movement is restricted. This leads to a decrease in the entropy of the gas i.e. $\Delta S$ is negative. Now, for a process to be spontaneous, $\Delta G$ should be negative.
We know that, $\Delta G=\Delta H-T \Delta S$
Now, $\Delta S$ is negative, $\Delta H$ has to be negative to make $\Delta G$ negative. Hence, adsorption is always exothermic.
5793.meta: Assertion (A) Adsorption is an exothermic process. Reason (R) Physisorption of a gas on a solid surface is normally reversible.

& $\mathrm{C}$($\mathrm{g}$)+$\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g}$) \longrightarrow $\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{~g}$) ; \Delta $\mathrm{H}=\text{ ? }$\\
&

On adding Eqs (i), (ii)$ and $(iii), we get Eq (iv)

\begin{aligned}
&$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$($\mathrm{g}$)+$\mathrm{C}$($\mathrm{g}$) \longrightarrow $\mathrm{CO}$(g)+$\mathrm{H}_2(g)$ ; \\
& \Delta H=+131 $\mathrm{~kJ}$ \\
& $\mathrm{CO}$($\mathrm{g}$)+$\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g}$) \longrightarrow $\mathrm{CO}_2(g)$ \\
& \Delta H=-282 $\mathrm{~kJ}$ \\
& $\mathrm{H}_2(g)+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_2($g) \longrightarrow $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$(g) $\text{; }$ \\

& $\mathrm{C}$($\mathrm{g}$)+$\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g})$\longrightarrow $\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \\

& =-393 \mathrm{~kJ} \\

$

$$

$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad 0 \geq-\frac{\sin ^2 2 x}{4} \geq-\frac{1}{4} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 1 \geq 1-\frac{\sin ^2 2 x}{4} \geq-\frac{1}{4} \\
& 1 \geq 1-\frac{\sin ^2 2 x}{4} \geq-\frac{1}{4}+1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 1 \geq 1-\frac{\sin ^2 2 x}{4} \geq \frac{3}{4} \\
&
\end{aligned}
$$
Range of $f=\left[\frac{3}{4}, 1\right]$

10706.text: A bag contains 4 red and 3 black balls. A second bag contains 2 red and 3 black balls. One bag is selected at random. If from the selected bag, one ball is drawn at random, then the probability that the ball drawn is red, is
10706.sol:
A red ball can be drawn in two mutually exclusive ways.
(i) Selecting bag I and then drawing a red ball from it.
(ii) Selecting bag II and then drawing a red ball from it
Let $E_1^{\prime}, E_2$ and A$ denote the events defined as follows
\begin{aligned} & E_1=\text{ Selecting bag I } \\ & E_2=\text{ Selecting bag II }\end{aligned}$
Since, one of the two bags is selected randomly.
$\therefore P\left(E_1\right)=\frac{1}{2} and P\left(E_2\right)=\frac{1}{2}$
Now, $P\left(\frac{A}{E_1}\right)=$ Probability of drawing a red ball
when the first bag has been selected $=4 / 7P\left(\frac{A}{E_2}\right)=$ Probability of drawing a red ball when
the second bag has been selected $=2 / 5P($ red ball $)=P\left(E_1\right) P\left(\frac{A}{E_1}\right)+P\left(E_2\right) P\left(\frac{A}{E_2}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{7}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{5}=\frac{2}{7}+\frac{1}{5}=\frac{17}{35}$

11202.sol:
We know that, $\begin{aligned}& r=4 R \sin \frac{A}{2} \sin \frac{B}{2} \sin \frac{C}{2}\\
& r_1=4 R \sin \frac{A}{2} \cos \frac{B}{2} \cos \frac{C}{2}\\

& \Rightarrow \quad r_3-r=r_1+r_2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 4 R \sin \frac{C}{2} \left(\cos \frac{A}{2} \cos \frac{B}{2}-\sin \frac{B}{2} \sin \frac{A}{2}\right)\\
& =4 R \cos \frac{C}{2} \left[\sin \frac{A}{2} \cos \frac{B}{2}+\cos \frac{A}{2} \sin \frac{B}{2}\right]\\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sin \frac{C}{2} \left(\cos \left(\frac{A+B}{2}\right)\right)=\cos \frac{C}{2}\left(\sin \left(\frac{A+B}{2}\right)\right)\\
& \Rightarrow \sin \frac{C}{2}\left(\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{C}{2}\right)\right)=\cos \frac{C}{2} \left(\sin \ \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{C}{2}\right)\right) \\
& {\left[\because A+B+C=\pi \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}+\frac{B}{2}=\frac{\pi}{2}- C\right]} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sin ^2\frac{A}{2}=\cos ^ 2 \frac{C}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \tan\frac{C}{2}=1 \\
&
\end{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad \frac{C}{2}=\frac{\pi}{4}$ \Rightarrow C=$\frac{\pi}{2}$ We know that, A+B+C=\pi $\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow& A+B=\pi-\frac{\pi}{2}$ \\
\Rightarrow & A+B=$\frac{\pi}{2}
\end{array}$

11365.sol:
$Q(x)$ be a polynomial of degree $n$.

Q(1)=1 $\text{$ and $} \frac{Q(2 x)}{Q(x+1)}+\frac{56}{x+7}-8=0...(i)

Put$ x=0 in $Eq. (i), we get

\begin{aligned}\frac{Q(0)}{Q(1)}+\frac{56}{7}-8 & =0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{Q(0)}{1}+8-8 & =0 \\
Q(0) & =0
\end{aligned}

Solving Eq. (i), we get

\begin{aligned}$& $\frac{Q(2 x)}{Q(x+1)}+\frac{56-8 x-56}{x+7}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{Q(2 x)}{Q(x+1)}-\frac{8 x}{x+7}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{Q(2 x)}{Q(x+1)}=\frac{8 x}{x+7}...($ ii) \\
& \because \quad Q(0)=0 \\
&
\end{aligned}

$\therefore \quad x$ is a factor of $Q(x)$.
Let $Q(x)=x P(x)$
\therefore \quad $\begin{aligned}\frac{Q(2 x)}{Q(x+1)}$& =$\frac{8 x}{x+7}$\\
$\frac{2 x \cdot P(2 x)}{(x+1) P(x+1)}$& =$\frac{8 x}{x+7}$\\
$\frac{P(2 x)}{P(x+1}$& =$\frac{4(x+1)}{x+7}...($ ii)
\end{aligned}

Put $ x=-1\frac{P(-2)}{P(0)}=0 \Rightarrow P(-2)=0

$\Rightarrow \quad x+2$ is factor of $P(x)P(x)=(x+2) R(x)

Now, in $Eq, (ii), we get

\begin{aligned}\frac{4(x+1)}{x+7}$& =$\frac{P(2 x)}{P(x+1)}=\frac{(2 x+2) R(2 x)}{(x+1+2) R(x+1)}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{4(x+1)}{x+7}$& =$\frac{2 x+2}{x+3} \frac{R(2 x)}{R(x+1)}$\\
$\frac{2(x+3)}{x+7}$& =$\frac{R(2 x)}{R(x+1)}$\\
\because \quad x & =-3 \Rightarrow 0=$\frac{R(-6)}{R(-2)} \Rightarrow$ R(-6)=0
\end{aligned}

$=x+6$ is a factor of $R(x)$.
So, $R(x)=(x+6) S(x) \begin{aligned}\frac{2(x+3)}{x+7}$& =$\frac{R(2 x)}{R(x+1)}=\frac{(2 x+6) S(2 x)}{(x+6+1) S(x+1)}$\\
\Rightarrow & $\frac{S(2 x)}{S(x+1)}=1 \Rightarrow S(2 x)=S(x+1) \text{$ for all } x
\end{aligned}$\Rightarrow S(x)$ is constant function.

\therefore Q(x)=x P(x)=x(x+2) R(x)=x(x+2)(x+3) S(x)

$\therefore Q(x)$ is cubic polynomial.

$\begin{aligned}$& \therefore n=3 \\
& $\begin{aligned}\text{ Required value }$& ={ }^3 C_0+{ }^3 C_1+{ }^3 C_2+{ }^3 C_3 \\
& =1+3+3+1=8
\end{aligned}
\end{aligned}

20118.subject: Chemistry
20118.text: Which of the following is always true about a spontaneous cell reaction in a galvanic cell?
20118.sol:
For a spontaneous cell reaction, the change in Gibbs free energy must be negative, i.e., $\Delta G < 0$.

The relationship between $\Delta G$, the standard Gibbs free energy change $\Delta G^o$, and the reaction quotient $Q_C$ is given by:
$\Delta G = \Delta G^o + RT \ln Q_C$

At equilibrium, $\Delta G = 0$ and Q_C = K_C, so:
$\Delta G^o = -RT \ln K_C$

Substituting this back into the first equation, we get:
$\Delta G = -RT \ln K_C + RT \ln Q_C = RT \ln \left( \dfrac{Q_C}{K_C} \right)

For the reaction to be spontaneous (\Delta$ G < 0$), we must have:
$RT \ln $\left( \dfrac{Q_C}{K_C} \right) <0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{Q_C}{K_C} <1 \Rightarrow Q_C < K_C$

In a standard galvanic cell, the standard cell potential is positive, $E^o_{cell} > 0$.
Since \Delta$ G^o = -nFE^o_{cell}$, a positive $E^o_{cell}$ implies that \Delta$ G^o < 0$.

Therefore, the correct conditions are $E^o_{cell} > 0$, \Delta$ G^o < 0$, and $Q_C < K_C$.

Answer: $E^o_{cell} > 0;\ $\Delta$ G^o < 0;\ Q_C < K_C$

20385.subject: Chemistry
20385.text: Identify the type of reaction:
20385.sol:
The reaction shown is the addition of hydrogen bromide (HBr) to propene (CH_3-CH=CH_2$).

The reaction proceeds via the electrophilic addition mechanism. In the first step, the electrophile $H^{+}$ from HBr attacks the double bond to form the more stable secondary carbocation (CH_3-CH^{+}-CH_3$).

In the second step, the nucleophile $Br^{-}$ attacks the carbocation to form 2-bromopropane (CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_3$).

This follows Markovnikov's rule, which is characteristic of electrophilic addition reactions to alkenes.

Answer: Electrophilic addition$

20415.text:
The conversion of Propyne to Benzene can be brought out in 4 steps.
Choose the reagents to be used, in the proper sequential order, to bring out the conversion.
Reagents provided: alc. $\mathrm{KOH}, \mathrm{H}_2 / \mathrm{Pd}, \mathrm{Na} /$ dry ether, $\mathrm{HBr}, \mathrm{HBr} /\left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CO}\right)_2 \mathrm{O}_2$,
Soda-lime, $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ (high T and P), Conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$
20415.sol:
The conversion of propyne ($CH_3-C \equiv CH$) to benzene ($C_6H_6$) involves the following steps:

Partial hydrogenation of propyne to propene using $H_2 / Pd$ (Lindlar catalyst or poisoned Pd).
$CH_3-C \equiv CH + H_2 \xrightarrow{Pd} CH_3-CH=CH_2$

Anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr to propene using peroxide ($HBr / (C_6H_5CO)_2O_2$) to obtain 1-bromopropane.
$CH_3-CH=CH_2 + HBr \xrightarrow{peroxide} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2Br$

Wurtz reaction using $Na / dry ether$ to convert 1-bromopropane to n-hexane.
$2 CH_3-CH_2-CH_2Br + 2 Na \xrightarrow{dry ether} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$

Aromatization of n-hexane to benzene using $Cr_2O_3$ at high temperature and pressure.
$CH_3(CH_2)_4CH_3 \xrightarrow{Cr_2O_3, \Delta, P} C_6H_6 + 4H_2$

Answer: $\mathrm{H}_2 / \mathrm{Pd}, \mathrm{HBr} /\left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CO}\right)_2 \mathrm{O}_2, \mathrm{Na} /$ dry ether, $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ (high $\mathrm{T}$ and $\mathrm{P}$)

21430.subject: Mathematics
21430.text: The equation of an ellipse, whose focus is $(1,0)$, directrix is $x=4$ and whose eccentricity is a root of the quadratic equation $2 x^2-3 x+1=0$, is
21430.sol:
The given quadratic equation is $2e^2 - 3e + 1 = 0$. Solving for $e$:

$2e^2 - 2e - e + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow 2e(e - 1) - 1(e - 1) = 0 \Rightarrow (2e - 1)(e - 1) = 0$.

The roots are $e = 1$ or $e = 1/2$. Since the curve is an ellipse, $e < 1$, so $e = 1/2$.

Let the focus be $S(1, 0)$ and the directrix be $x = 4$. By the definition of a conic section, for any point $P(x, y)$ on the ellipse, $SP^2 = e^2 PM^2$, where $PM$ is the perpendicular distance from $P$ to the directrix $x - 4 = 0$.

$(x - 1)^2 + (y - 0)^2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 (x - 4)^2$

$(x - 1)^2 + y^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} (x^2 - 8x + 16)$

$4(x^2 - 2x + 1 + y^2) = x^2 - 8x + 16$

$4x^2 - 8x + 4 + 4y^2 = x^2 - 8x + 16$

$3x^2 + 4y^2 = 12$

Dividing by 12, we get $\dfrac{x^2}{4} + \dfrac{y^2}{3} = 1$.

Answer: $\dfrac{x^2}{4}+\dfrac{y^2}{3}=1$

Let $I = \int \dfrac{e^{\tan^{-1} x}}{1+x^2} (1+x+x^2) dx$.

Substitute $t = \tan^{-1} x$, so $dt = \dfrac{1}{1+x^2} dx$.

Then $x = \tan t$. The integral becomes $I = \int e^t (1 + \tan t + \tan^2 t) dt$.

Using the identity $1 + \tan^2 t = \sec^2 t$, we have $I = \int e^t (\sec^2 t + \tan t) dt$.

Recall the standard integral form $\int e^t (f(t) + f'(t)) dt = e^t f(t) + c$.

Here, let $f(t) = \tan t$, then $f'(t) = \sec^2 t$.

Thus, $I = e^t \tan t + c$.

Substituting back $t = \tan^{-1} x$ and $\tan t = x$, we get $I = e^{\tan^{-1} x} \cdot x + c$.

Answer: $x e^{\tan ^{-1} x}+c$

21537.sol:
Let $z_1 = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \dfrac{i}{2} = \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) + i\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = e^{i\pi/6}$.

Let $z_2 = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \dfrac{i}{2} = \cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) + i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = e^{-i\pi/6}$.

The given expression is $z = z_1^5 + z_2^5$.

Using De Moivre's Theorem, $z_1^5 = \cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) + i\sin\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)$ and $z_2^5 = \cos\left(-\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) + i\sin\left(-\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)$.

Since $\cos(-\theta) = \cos(\theta)$ and $\sin(-\theta) = -\sin(\theta)$, we have $z_2^5 = \cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) - i\sin\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)$.

Adding these, $z = 2\cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) + i\left(\sin\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) - \sin\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)\right) = 2\cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)$.

Since $\cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, we get $z = 2\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -\sqrt{3}$.

Thus, $\operatorname{Re}(z) = -\sqrt{3}$ and $\operatorname{Im}(z) = 0$.

Answer: $\operatorname{Im}(z)=0$

21668.text: The value of $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\dfrac{a^{x}+b^{x}+c^{x}}{3}\right)^{2 / x},(a, b, c > 0)$ is
21668.sol:
As $x \to 0$, the base $\dfrac{a^x+b^x+c^x}{3} \to 1$ and exponent $\dfrac{2}{x} \to \infty$, giving $1^\infty$ indeterminate form.

Using $\lim f(x)^{g(x)} = e^{\lim g(x)[f(x)-1]}$:

$L = e^{\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{2}{x}\left(\dfrac{a^x+b^x+c^x}{3}-1\right)} = e^{\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{2}{3}\left(\dfrac{a^x+b^x+c^x-3}{x}\right)}$

$= e^{\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{2}{3}\left(\dfrac{a^x-1}{x}+\dfrac{b^x-1}{x}+\dfrac{c^x-1}{x}\right)}$

Using $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{k^x - 1}{x} = \ln k$:

$L = e^{\dfrac{2}{3}(\ln a + \ln b + \ln c)} = e^{\dfrac{2}{3}\ln(abc)} = e^{\ln(abc)^{2/3}} = (abc)^{2/3}$

This does not match options (1), (2), or (3). The answer is (4) None of these.

21851.subject: Mathematics
21851.text: A polygon of n sides has 90 diagonals, then n is equal to
21851.sol:
The formula for number of diagonals in a polygon of $n$ sides is $D = \dfrac{n(n-3)}{2}$

Setting $D = 90$:

$\dfrac{n(n-3)}{2} = 90$

$n^2 - 3n - 180 = 0$

$(n-15)(n+12) = 0$

$n = 15$ or $n = -12$

Since $n$ must be a positive integer, $n = 15$.

21988.subject: Mathematics
21988.text: $0.2+0.22+0.022+\ldots \ldots \ldots$ up to $n$ terms is equal to
21988.sol:
The given series is $S_n = 0.2 + 0.22 + 0.222 + \ldots$ up to $n$ terms.

We can write each term as $T_k = 2 \times (0.1 + 0.01 + 0.001 + \ldots + 10^{-k}) = 2 \times \sum_{i=1}^{k} 10^{-i}$.

Alternatively, express the terms as $T_k = \dfrac{2}{10} + \dfrac{22}{100} + \dfrac{222}{1000} + \ldots = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \dfrac{2}{9} (1 - 10^{-k})$.

Expanding the summation, we get $S_n = \dfrac{2}{9} \sum_{k=1}^{n} (1 - 10^{-k}) = \dfrac{2}{9} \left( \sum_{k=1}^{n}1 - \sum_{k=1}^{n} 10^{-k} \right)$.

The sum $\sum_{k=1}^{n} 1 = n$.

The sum $\sum_{k=1}^{n} 10^{-k}$ is a geometric progression with first term $a = 0.1$ and common ratio $r = 0.1$.

Using the sum formula for a geometric progression, $\sum_{k=1}^{n} 10^{-k} = \dfrac{0.1(1 - (0.1)^n)}{1 - 0.1} = \dfrac{0.1(1 - 10^{-n})}{0.9} = \dfrac{1}{9}(1 - 10^{-n})$.

Substituting these back into the expression for $S_n$, we get $S_n = \dfrac{2}{9}\left[ n - \dfrac{1}{9}(1 - 10^{-n}) \right]$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{9} \left[n-\dfrac{1}{9} \left(1-10^{-n}\right)\right]$

23379.text: A person has a normal near point $25 \mathrm{ cm}$. What is the magnifying power of the simple microscope he used, if the focal length of the convex lens used is $10 \mathrm{ cm}$ and the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision?
23379.sol:
The magnifying power $M$ of a simple microscope when the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision $D$ is given by the formula:

$M = 1 + \dfrac{D}{f}$

Given values are:
Least distance of distinct vision $D = 25 \text{ cm}$
Focal length of the convex lens $f = 10 \text{ cm}$

Substituting these values into the formula:

$M = 1 + \dfrac{25}{10}$

$M = 1 + 2.5$

$M = 3.5$

Answer: 3.5

(c) $2{PbSO}_{4}\left(s\right) + 2{H}_{2}O\left(l\right) \to Pb\left(s\right) + {PbO}_{2}\left(s\right) + 2{H}_{2}{SO}_{4}\left(aq\right)$ Charging of secondary Battery

(d) $2{H}_{2}\left(g\right) + {O}_{2}\left(g\right) \to 2{H}_{2}O\left(l\right) -$ Fuel cell

Mercury cell, suitable for low current devices like hearing aids, watches, etc. consists of zinc - mercury amalgam as anode and a paste of $HgO$ and carbon as the cathode. The electrolyte is a paste of $KOH$ and $ZnO$. The electrode reactions for the cell are given below:

Anode: $Zn\left(Hg\right) + 2{OH}^{-} \to ZnO\left(s\right) + {H}_{2}O + 2{e}^{-}$

Cathode: $HgO + {H}_{2}O + 2{e}^{-} \to Hg\left(l\right) + 2{OH}^{-}$

Another important secondary cell is the nickel-cadmium cell which has longer life than the lead storage cell but more expensive to manufacture.

The overall reaction during discharge is:

$Cd\left(s\right) + 2Ni{\left(OH\right)}_{3}\left(s\right) \to CdO\left(s\right) + 2Ni{\left(OH\right)}_{2}\left(s\right) + {H}_{2}O\left(l\right)$

Cathode: ${O}_{2}\left(g\right) + 2{H}_{2}O\left(l\right) + 4{e}^{-} \to 4{OH}^{-}\left(aq\right)$

Anode: $2{H}_{2}\left(g\right) + 4{OH}^{-}\left(aq\right) \to 4{H}_{2}O\left(l\right) + 4{e}^{-}$

Overall reaction being:

$2{H}_{2}\left(g\right) + {O}_{2}\left(g\right) \to 2{H}_{2}O\left(l\right)$

(ii) Cell reaction of lead storage battery during recharge -

The reverse of oxidation at anode during discharge is the reduction reaction at cathode during recharging.

${Pb}_{\left(aq\right)}^{2 +} + 2{e}^{-} \to {Pb}_{\left(s\right)}$

${PbSO}_{4\left(s\right)} \to {Pb}_{\left(aq\right)}^{2 +} + {SO}_{4\left(aq\right)}^{2 -}$

33552.subject: Mathematics
33552.text: Let a circle $C$ have its centre in the first quadrant, intersect the coordinate axes at exactly three points and cut off equal intercepts from the coordinate axes. If the length of the chord of $C$ on the line $x + y = 1$ is $\sqrt{14}$, then the square of the radius of $C$ is _______.
33552.sol:
Let the equation of the circle be $x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$.

Since the circle intersects the coordinate axes at exactly three points, it must pass through the origin and intersect each axis at one other distinct point. Thus, $c = 0$.

The lengths of the intercepts on the x-axis and y-axis are $2\sqrt{g^2 - c} = 2|g|$ and $2\sqrt{f^2 - c} = 2|f|$.

Given that the intercepts are equal, we have $|g| = |f|$.

The centre of the circle is $(-g, -f)$. Since it lies in the first quadrant, $-g > 0$ and $-f > 0$. Therefore, $g = f = -a$ for some $a > 0$.

The centre is $(a, a)$ and the radius is $r = \sqrt{a^2 + a^2} = a\sqrt{2}$.

The distance $d$ from the centre $(a, a)$ to the line $x + y - 1 = 0$ is given by:

$d = \dfrac{|a + a - 1|}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2}} = \dfrac{|2a - 1|}{\sqrt{2}}$

The length of the chord on the given line is $2\sqrt{r^2 - d^2} = \sqrt{14}$.

Squaring both sides, we get:

$4(r^2 - d^2) = 14 \Rightarrow r^2 - d^2 = \dfrac{7}{2}$

Substituting $r^2 = 2a^2$ and $d^2 = \dfrac{(2a - 1)^2}{2}$:

$2a^2 - \dfrac{(2a - 1)^2}{2} = \dfrac{7}{2}$

$4a^2 - (4a^2 - 4a + 1) = 7$

$4a - 1 = 7 \Rightarrow 4a = 8 \Rightarrow a = 2$

The square of the radius of the circle is $r^2 = 2a^2 = 2(2)^2 = 8$.

Answer: $8$

34726.text: Let $y = y ( x )$  be the solution of the differential equation $x{\log}_{e}x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = {x}^{2}{\log}_{e}x, ( x > 1 )$. If $y ( 2 ) = 2$, then $y ( e )$ is equal to
34726.sol:
Given,

$xlnx\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = {x}^{2}lnx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{xlnx} = x$

This is a linear differential equation.

Now, finding integrating factor we get

$I . F = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{1}{xlnx}dx} = {e}^{ln\left(lnx\right)} = lnx$

Now, solution of the differential equation is given by

$y \times I . F = ∫ \left(x \times I . F\right)dx$

$⇒ y \times lnx = ∫ xlnxdx$

$⇒ y \times lnx = lnx \cdot \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} + c$

Now given $y\left(2\right) = 2$,

$2 \times ln2 = ln2 \cdot \dfrac{{2}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{2}^{2}}{4} + c$

$⇒ c = 1$

So, equation will be $y \times lnx = lnx \cdot \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} + 1$

Now finding $y\left(e\right)$ we get,

$y \times lne = lne \cdot \dfrac{{e}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{e}^{2}}{4} + 1$

$⇒ y \times 1 = 1 \cdot \dfrac{{e}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{e}^{2}}{4} + 1$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{4 + {e}^{2}}{4}$

35039.text: If the curves, $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{a} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{b} = 1$ and $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{c} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{d} = 1$ intersect each other at an angle of ${90}^{°},$ then which of the following relations is TRUE?
35039.sol:
Given curves, $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{a} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{b} = 1 . . . . . \left(i\right)$

On differentiating equation $\left(i\right)$, we get

$\dfrac{2x}{a} + \dfrac{2y}{b}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ {m}_{1} = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \dfrac{xb}{ya} . . . \left(iii\right)$

and $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{c} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{d} = 1 . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

On differentiating equation $\left(ii\right)$, we get

$\dfrac{2x}{c} + \dfrac{2y}{d}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ {m}_{2} = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \dfrac{xd}{yc} . . . \left(iv\right)$

For orthogonal curves, ${m}_{1} \times {m}_{2} = - 1$

$⇒ \left(- \dfrac{xb}{ya}\right) \times \left(- \dfrac{xd}{yc}\right) = - 1$

$\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}} = - \dfrac{ac}{bd} . . . . \left(v\right)$

From equation $\left(i\right) - \left(ii\right)$, we get

${x}^{2}\left(\dfrac{c - a}{ac}\right) = {y}^{2}\left(\dfrac{b - d}{bd}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}} = \left(\dfrac{b - d}{c - a}\right)\left(\dfrac{ac}{bd}\right)$

From equation $\left(v\right)$, we get

$a - c = b - d$

$⇒ a - b = c - d$.

$= \lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{\sqrt{2}\left[\left(1 - \dfrac{sinx}{cosx}\right)\left(1 + tanx\right){sec}^{2}x\right]}{\tan^{3}x . \left(cosx - sinx\right)}$

$= \lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{\sqrt{2}\left(cosx - sinx\right) . \left(1 + tanx\right) . se{c}^{2}x}{cosx . ta{n}^{3}x . \left(cosx - sinx\right)}$

$= \dfrac{\sqrt{2}\left(1 + tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}{\sin^{3}\dfrac{\pi}{4}}$

$= 8$.

Let $A$, be a $3 \times 3$ matrix, such that ${A}^{2} - 5A + 7I = O .$
Statement - I : ${A}^{- 1} = \dfrac{1}{7}\left(5I - A\right) .$

${A}^{2} = 5A - 7I . . . . . \left(i\right)

$AI = 5I - 7{A}^{- 1}$

$= A$\left(5A - 7I\right)$ - 2{A}^{2} - 3A + I$ {from\left(i\right)}

$= 5{A}^{2} - 7A - 2{A}^{2} - 3A + I$

$= 3{A}^{2} - 10A + I$

$= 3$\left(5A - 7I\right)$ - 10A + I$ {from\left(i\right)}

$= 5A - 20I$

$= 5$\left(A - 4I\right)$

Hence, Statement II is true.

37171.text: If $\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}\dfrac{k}{{k}^{4} + {k}^{2} + 1} = \dfrac{m}{n}$, where $m$ and $n$ are co-prime, then $m + n$ is equal to
37171.sol:
Given,

$\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}\dfrac{k}{{k}^{4} + {k}^{2} + 1} = \dfrac{m}{n}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}\dfrac{\left({k}^{2} + k + 1\right) - \left({k}^{2} - k + 1\right)}{\left({k}^{2} + k + 1\right)\left({k}^{2} - k + 1\right)} = \dfrac{m}{n}$

$\left\{\text{by using$ the $formula}{x}^{4} + {x}^{2} + 1 = \left({x}^{2} + x + 1\right)\left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right)\right\}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}\left(\dfrac{1}{\left({k}^{2} - k + 1\right)} - \dfrac{1}{{k}^{2} + k + 1}\right)\right) = \dfrac{m}{n}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{7} + \dfrac{1}{7} - . . . . . . . . . - \dfrac{1}{111}\right) = \dfrac{m}{n}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{111}\right) = \dfrac{m}{n}$

$⇒ \dfrac{55}{111} = \dfrac{m}{n}$

So, $m + n = 166$

38042.text: The plane $2 x-y+z=4$ intersects the line segment joining the points $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{a},-2,4)$ and $\mathrm{B}(2, \mathrm{~b},-3)$ at the point $\mathrm{C}$ in the ratio $2: 1$ and the distance of the point $\mathrm{C}$ from the origin is $\sqrt{5}$. Given points are:

$A ( a, - 2, 4 )$ and $B ( 2, b, - 3 )$

Point $C$ divides the line segment joining points $A$ and $B$ in the ratio $2: 1$, so

$C ≡ \left(\dfrac{a + 4}{3}, \dfrac{2b - 2}{3}, - \dfrac{2}{3}\right)$

Also, $C$ lies on $2x - y + 2 = 4$, therefore

$\dfrac{2a + 8}{3} - \left(\dfrac{2b - 2}{3}\right) - \dfrac{2}{3} = 4$

$⇒ 2a + 8 - 2b + 2 - 2 = 12$

$⇒ a - b = 2 . . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, $OC = \sqrt{5}$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{a + 4}{3}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{2b - 2}{3}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{4}{9} = 5$

$⇒ {a}^{2} + 8a + 4{b}^{2} - 8b = 25 . . . \left(2\right)$

Solving $\left(1\right)$ and $( 2 )$, we have

$( b + 6{)}^{2} + ( 2b - 2{)}^{2} = 41$

$⇒ 5{b}^{2} + 4b - 1 = 0$

$⇒ b = - 1$ or $\dfrac{1}{5}$

$⇒ a = 1$ or $\dfrac{11}{5}$

But $ab < 0 ⇒ \left(a, b\right) ≡ \left(1, - 1\right)$

$C ≡ \left(\dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{- 4}{3}, \dfrac{- 2}{3}\right), P ≡ ( 2, - 1, - 3 )$

$C{P}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{49}{9} = \dfrac{51}{9} = \dfrac{17}{3}$

38047.subject: Mathematics
38047.text: The foot of perpendicular of the point $\left(2, 0, 5\right)$ on the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{5} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 1}$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$. Then. Which of the following is NOT correct?
38047.sol:
Given line is

$L: \dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{5} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 1} = \lambda$ (let)

Let foot of perpendicular is $P\left(2\lambda - 1, 5\lambda + 1, - \lambda - 1\right)$

$\overset{\to}{PA} = \left(3 - 2\lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} - \left(5\lambda + 1\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(6 + \lambda\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Direction ratio of line is

$\overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

Now, $\overset{\to}{PA} ⊥ L$, so

$\overset{\to}{PA} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 0$

$⇒ 2\left(3 - 2\lambda\right) - 5\left(5\lambda + 1\right) - \left(6 + \lambda\right) = 0$

$⇒ 6 - 4\lambda - 25\lambda - 5 - 6 - \lambda = 0$

$⇒ - 30\lambda - 5 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - \dfrac{1}{6}$

So,

$P\left(2\lambda - 1, 5\lambda + 1, - \lambda - 1\right) ≡ P\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$

Now,

$\alpha = 2\left(- \dfrac{1}{6}\right) - 1 = - \dfrac{4}{3} ⇒ \alpha = - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$\beta = 5\left(- \dfrac{1}{6}\right) + 1 = \dfrac{1}{6} ⇒ \beta = \dfrac{1}{6}$

$\gamma = - \lambda - 1 = \dfrac{1}{6} - 1 ⇒ \gamma = - \dfrac{5}{6}$

So,

$\dfrac{\beta}{\gamma} = - \dfrac{1}{5} \ne - 5$

39252.text:
This question has Statement 1 and Statement 2 . Of the four choices given after the Statements, choose the one that best describes the two Statements.
Statement 1: It is not possible to make a sphere of capacity 1 farad using a conducting material. 
Statement 2: It is possible for earth as its radius is $6.4 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m}$.
options:
Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is true, Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1.

Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true.

Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is true, Statement 2 is not the correct explanation of Statement 1.

Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false.
39252.sol:
Capacitance of sphere is given by:
$C=4 \pi \epsilon_0 r$
If, $C=1 \mathrm{~F}$ then radius of sphere needed:
$r=\frac{C}{4 \pi \epsilon_0}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12}}$
or, $r=\frac{10^{12}}{4 \pi \times 8.85}=9 \times 10^9 \mathrm{~m}$
$9 \times 10^9 \mathrm{~m}$ is very large, it is not possible to obtain such a large sphere. Infact earth has radius $6.4 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m}$ only and capacitance of earth is $711 \mu \mathrm{F}$.

41910.text:
In the experiment for measurement of viscosity ' $\eta$ ' of given liquid with a ball having radius $R$, consider following statements.
A. Graph between terminal velocity V and R will be a parabola.
B. The terminal velocities of different diameter balls are constant for a given liquid.
C. Measurement of terminal velocity is dependent on the temperature.
D. This experiment can be utilized to assess the density of a given liquid.
E. If balls are dropped with some initial speed, the value of $\eta$ will change.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
41910.sol:
The terminal velocity of ball of radius $R$ inside a liquid of viscosity $\eta$ can be written as $V_T=\frac{2 R^2 g}{n}(\sigma-\rho)$, where $\sigma$ is the density of ball and $\delta$ is the density of the liquid.
Hence,
$A$ is correct since $V_T \propto R^2$ gives a parabola on a graph
$C$ is correct since $V_T \alpha \frac{1}{\eta}$ and $\eta$ varies with temperature
$D$ is correct since $V_T \alpha(\sigma-\rho)$ i.e., varies with density of liquid.

42946.text: A bi convex lens of focal length $10cm$ is cut in two identical parts along a plane perpendicular to the principal axis. The power of each lens after cut is _____ $D$.
42946.sol:
The focal length of the bi-convex lens $\left(f\right)$ can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{f} & = & ( \mu - 1 ) \left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{- R}\right) \\ & = & \dfrac{2\left(\mu - 1\right)}{R} . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

When the lens is cut into two halves, the focal length $\left(f '\right)$ of each part can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{{f}^{'}} & = & ( \mu - 1 ) \left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right) \\ & = & \dfrac{\left(\mu - 1\right)}{R} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Hence, the ratio of the powers for both the lenses can be given by

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{{P}^{'}}{P} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{f '}}{\dfrac{1}{f}} \\ & = & \dfrac{f}{f '} \\ & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{\left(\mu - 1\right)}{R}}{\dfrac{2\left(\mu - 1\right)}{R}} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{2} \\ & ⇒ & P ' = \dfrac{P}{2} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the value of the known parameter into equation (3) to calculate the required power.

$\begin{cases}P ' & = & \dfrac{10D}{2} \\ & = & 5D\end{cases}$

When light travels through a medium, its velocity depends on the density of the medium.

Because of changed wavelength the phase difference changes while the two waves travel the same distance.

44014.subject: Physics
44014.text:
This question has Statement 1 and Statement 2. Of the four choices given after the Statements, choose the one that best describes the two Statements.
Statement 1: An inventor claims to have constructed an engine that has an efficiency of $30 \%$ when operated between the boiling and freezing points of water. This is not possible.
Statement 2: The efficiency of a real engine is always less than the efficiency of a Carnot engine operating between the same two temperatures.
options:
Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is true, Statement 2 is not the correct explanation of Statement 1.

Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false.

Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true.

Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is true, Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1.
44014.sol:
According to Carnot's theorem - no heat engine working between two given temperatures of source and sink can be more efficient than a perfectly reversible engine i.e. Carnot engine working between the same two temperatures.
Efficiency of Carnot's engine, $n=1-\frac{T_2}{T_1}$ where, $T_1=$ temperature of source $T_2=$ temperature of sink

44516.text: A source of sound A emitting waves of frequency $1800 \mathrm{~Hz}$ is falling towards ground with a terminal speed $\mathrm{v}$. The observer $\mathrm{B}$ on the ground directly beneath the source receives waves of frequency $2150 \mathrm{~Hz}$. Given $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{A}}=1800 \mathrm{~Hz} \begin{aligned}$&$\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{v}$\\
&$\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{B}}=$2150 $\mathrm{~Hz}
\end{aligned}$Reflected wave frequency received by $\mathrm{A}$, $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{A}}{ }^{\prime}=$ ?
Applying doppler's effect of sound, $\mathrmf^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{s}} \mathrm{f}}{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{s}}-\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{t}}}$
Here, $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{s}}\left(1-\frac{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{B}}}\right)=343\left(1-\frac{1800}{2150}\right)\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{t}}=55.8372 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
Now, for the reflected wave,

$\begin{aligned}$&\therefore $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{A}}{ }^{\prime}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{s}}+\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{s}}-\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{t}}}\right) \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{A}}$\\
&=$\left(\frac{343+55.83}{343-55.83}\right) \times$1800 \\
&=2499.44 $\approx$2500 $\mathrm{~Hz}
\end{aligned}$

50501.subject: Physics
50501.text:
Mass number of the elements A, B, C and D are $30,60,90$ and 120 respectively. The specific binding energy of them are $5 \mathrm{MeV}, 8.5 \mathrm{MeV}$, $8 \mathrm{MeV}$ and $7 \mathrm{MeV}$ respectively. Then, in which of the following reaction/s energy is released?
1. $\mathrm{D} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{~B}$
2. $\mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}+\mathrm{A}$
3. $\mathrm{B} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{~A}$
50501.sol:
(1) $\Delta \mathrm{E}=2 \times 60 \times 8.5-120 \times 7=180 \mathrm{MeV}$
(2) $\Delta \mathrm{E}=60 \times 8.5+30 \times 5-90 \times 8=-60 \mathrm{MeV}$
(3) $\Delta \mathrm{E}=2 \times 30 \times 5-60 \times 8.5=-105 \mathrm{MeV}$
Hence, energy is released in (1) only.
So, option (b) is correct.

50636.subject: Physics
50636.text: A coin placed on a rotating turn table just slips if it is placed at a distance of $4 \mathrm{ cm}$ from the centre. If the angular velocity of the turn table is doubled it will just slip at a distance of
50636.sol:
When the coin placed on a rotating table is first about to slips, then till the time the coin rotates along with the table, necessary centripetal force for rotation will be provided by the frictional force,
i.e., $\quad m r \omega^{2}=\mu m g$
where,
$m=$ mass of the coin,
$r=$ distance of the coin from the centre of the table,
$\omega=$ angular velocity,
$\mu=$ coefficient of friction
and $g=$ acceleration due to gravity.
Since, $m, \mu$ and $g$ remains constant, so
$r \omega^{2}=$ constant
$\Rightarrow \quad r \propto \frac{1}{\omega^{2}}$
or $\quad \frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}=\left(\frac{\omega_{1}}{\omega_{2}}\right)^{2}$
Given, $\omega_{2}=2 \omega_{1}, r_{1}=4 \mathrm{ cm}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}=\left(\frac{\omega_{1}}{2 \omega_{1}}\right)^{2}$
or
$r_{2}=\frac{r_{1}}{4}=\frac{4}{4}=1 \mathrm{ cm}$

52465.text:
A certain tiquid has a melting point of $- 50 ° C$ and a boiling point of $150 ° C$. A thermometer is designed with this liquid and its melting and boiling points are designated at $0 ° L$ and $100 ° L$. The melting and boiling points of water on this scale are
&
52465.sol:
From principle of thermometry,

$\dfrac{T - {T}_{LFP}}{{T}_{UFP} - {T}_{LFP}} = a$ constant for every

thermometric scale.
Now, for any temperature $L$ on a thermometer designed with given liquid and equivalent temperature $C$ on centigrade scale, we have

$\left(\dfrac{L - {T}_{LF}}{{T}_{UFP} - {T}_{LFP}}\right)\text{Liquid based scale} = \left(\dfrac{C - {T}_{LFP}}{{T}_{UFP} - {T}_{LFP}}\right)\text{Centigrade Scale}$

$⇒ \dfrac{L - ( - 50 )}{150 - ( - 50 )} = \dfrac{C - 0}{100 - 0}$

~

$\dfrac{L + 50}{150 + 50} = \dfrac{C}{100}$

~

$⇒ L + 50 = 2C$

Now at $0 ° L,$~centigrade scale reading will be

0 + 50 = 2C or $C = \dfrac{50}{2} = 25 ° L$

and at $100 ° L$, centigrade scale reading will be

100 + 50 = 2C or $C = \dfrac{150}{2} = 75 ° L$

54048.sol:
We know that a vector perpendicular to the plane containing the point $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and $\mathbf{C}$ is given by $\mathbf{A} \times \mathbf{B}+\mathbf{B} \times \mathbf{C}+\mathbf{C} \times \mathbf{A}$.
Given, $\mathbf{A}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}, \quad=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+0 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $\mathbf{C}=0 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Now, $\mathbf{A} \times \mathbf{B}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{array}\right|=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\mathbf{B} \times \mathbf{C}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{array}\right|=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\mathbf{C} \times \mathbf{A}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2\end{array}\right|=5 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Thus, $\mathbf{A} \times \mathbf{B}+\mathbf{B} \times \mathbf{C}+\mathbf{C} \times \mathbf{A}\begin{aligned} & =(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}})+(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}})+(5 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\ & =8 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\end{aligned}$

55259.text: Which of the following reactions uses diazonium salt ?
55259.sol:
The Sandmeyer reaction involves the conversion of an aryl diazonium salt into an aryl halide using copper(I) salts, such as $CuCl$ or $CuBr$.

The Mendius reaction is the reduction of nitriles to primary amines using sodium and ethanol.

The Hofmann rearrangement reaction involves the conversion of a primary amide to a primary amine with one fewer carbon atom using bromine and a strong base.

The carbylamine reaction is a test for primary amines, where a primary amine reacts with chloroform and a base to form an isocyanide.

Therefore, only the Sandmeyer reaction uses a diazonium salt.

Answer: Sandmeyer reaction

The d-block elements are distributed into four transition series based on the filling of d-orbitals:

First transition series (3d$ series): Sc (Z=21$) to Zn (Z=30$)

Second transition series (4d$ series): Y (Z=39$) to Cd (Z=48$)

Third transition series (5d$ series): La (Z=57$), Hf (Z=72$) to Hg (Z=80$)

Fourth transition series (6d$ series): Ac (Z=89$), Rf (Z=104$) to Cn (Z=112$)

Therefore, there are a total of $4$ transition series of d-block elements.

Answer: $4$

58252.subject: Chemistry
58252.text: Identify the correct order of thermal stability of hydrides of 16 group elements from the following.
58252.sol:
The thermal stability of Group 16 element hydrides is determined by the E–H bond strength, where E represents the central atom.

Bond strength decreases down the group due to increasing atomic size, which lengthens the bond and lowers the bond dissociation enthalpy. Weaker bonds dissociate more readily, reducing thermal stability.

The Group 16 elements in order of increasing atomic size are O < S < Se < Te, leading to the order of increasing E–H bond length: H–O < H–S < H–Se < H–Te. Consequently, bond strength decreases: H–O > H–S > H–Se > H–Te, and thermal stability follows the same decreasing order: $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} > \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S} > \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{Se} > \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{Te}$.

Expressed in increasing thermal stability: $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{Te} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{Se} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$.

Comparing with the options, only C matches this order: $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{Te} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{Se} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$.

Answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

59103.text:
Calculate van't Hoff factor for aqueous solution of 0.02 m formic acid if it freezes at -0.045 ^{}^{\circ}$\text{C} .
[K_f$ = 1.86 K kg $\text{mol}^{-1}$ and freezing point of water = 0\ ^{}^{\circ}$\text{C} ]$
59103.sol:
The depression in freezing point is given by $\Delta T_f = T_f^{}^{\circ} - T_f$.

$\Delta T_f = 0 - (-0.045) = 0.045 \text{ K}$

Using the formula for depression in freezing point:

$\Delta T_f = i \times K_f \times m$

Substituting the given values:

$0.045 = i \times 1.86 \times 0.02$

$0.045 = i \times 0.0372$

$i = \dfrac{0.045}{0.0372} = 1.209$

$i \approx 1.21$

Answer: $1.21$

59787.text: Identify example of sorption from following.

Oxygen gas is passed over finely divided nickel.
59787.sol:
Sorption describes the uptake of one substance by another, encompassing both adsorption and absorption. Adsorption involves accumulation on a surface, while absorption involves uniform distribution throughout a bulk material.

In the given examples: charcoal with methylene blue shows adsorption of dye molecules on the surface; chalk dipped in ink shows absorption as ink penetrates the bulk; hydrogen over platinum and oxygen over finely divided nickel both demonstrate adsorption of gases onto metal surfaces.

All processes are types of sorption.

62131.text: The X and Y intercepts of the tangent to the hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{20}-\frac{\mathrm{y}^2}{5}=1$ which is perpendicular to the line $4 x+3 y=7$, are respectively
62131.sol:
To determine the intercepts of the tangent to the hyperbola perpendicular to the line $4x+3y=7$, first note that the slope of the given line is $m_1 = -\frac{4}{3}$. Since the tangent is perpendicular, its slope is $m_2 = \frac{3}{4}$.

The standard form of the hyperbola is $\frac{x^2}{20} - \frac{y^2}{5} = 1$, implying $a^2 = 20$ and $b^2 = 5$. The equation for a tangent with slope $m$ is $y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^2 m^2 - b^2}$.
Substituting $m = \frac{3}{4}$ gives $y = \frac{3}{4}x \pm \sqrt{20 \cdot \frac{9}{16} - 5} = \frac{3}{4}x \pm \sqrt{\frac{45}{4} - \frac{20}{4}} = \frac{3}{4}x \pm \frac{5}{2}$.

Two tangents exist: $y = \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{2}$ and $y = \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{5}{2}$.
For $y = \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{2}$, the $y$-intercept is $\frac{5}{2}$ and the $x$-intercept is $-\frac{10}{3}$. For $y = \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{5}{2}$, the $y$-intercept is $-\frac{5}{2}$ and the $x$-intercept is $\frac{10}{3}$.

The intercepts match option B: $\frac{10}{3}$ and $-\frac{5}{2}$.

The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

62198.text: If $\int \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{2ax - x^2}} = f(g(x)) + c$, where $c$ is constant of integration, then $f(x), g(x)$ are respectively equal to
62198.sol:
The given integral is $I = \int \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{2ax - x^2}}$

Completing the square for the expression inside the square root:

$2ax - x^2 = a^2 - (x^2 - 2ax + a^2) = a^2 - (x - a)^2$

Substituting this back into the integral:

$I = \int \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{a^2 - (x - a)^2}}$

Using the standard integration formula $\int \dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{a^2 - t^2}} = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{t}{a}\right) + c$, we get:

$I = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x - a}{a}\right) + c$

Comparing this with $f(g(x)) + c$, we have:

$f(x) = \sin^{-1} x$

$g(x) = \dfrac{x - a}{a}$

Answer: $\sin^{-1} x, \dfrac{x - a}{a}$

65561.subject: Physics
65561.text: With gradual increase in frequency of an a.c. supply, the impedance of an LCR series circuit
options: first decreases, becomes minimum and then increases
65561.sol:
The impedance of an LCR series circuit is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$

where $X_L = 2\pi f L$ and $X_C = \dfrac{1}{2\pi f C}$.

At low frequencies, $X_C > X_L$, so the impedance is high.

As the frequency $f$ increases, $X_C$ decreases and $X_L$ increases, which reduces the magnitude of $(X_L - X_C)$. Thus, the impedance decreases.

At the resonant frequency $f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$, $X_L = X_C$, and the impedance becomes minimum, $Z = R$.

With a further increase in frequency, $X_L > X_C$, and the magnitude of $(X_L - X_C)$ increases, causing the impedance to increase.

Therefore, the impedance first decreases, becomes minimum, and then increases.

Answer: first decreases, becomes minimum and then increases

66347.text: If an ammeter is to be used in place of a galvanometer then we must connect
66347.sol:
A galvanometer must be converted into an ammeter by connecting a low resistance (shunt resistance $R_s$) in parallel. This configuration yields a low equivalent resistance, ensuring minimal disturbance to the circuit current. Most current flows through the shunt, protecting the galvanometer while allowing proportional deflection for measurement.

Series connection of either high or low resistance increases total resistance, making the device unsuitable as an ammeter. Parallel connection of a high resistance fails to achieve the necessary low resistance.

The correct choice is connecting a low resistance in parallel.

Final answer: $\boxed{A}$

67418.text: The mean kinetic energy of the molecules of an ideal gas at $399^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ is ' E '. The temperature at which the mean kinetic energy of its molecules will be ' $E / 2$ ', is
67418.sol:
The mean kinetic energy $E$ of an ideal gas is proportional to its absolute temperature, given by $E = \frac{3}{2} k_B T$, where $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant.

Given the initial temperature $399^{}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, convert to Kelvin: $T_1 = 399 + 273 = 672 \mathrm{K}$.

At temperature $T_1$, the energy is $E$; we seek the temperature $T_2$ for energy $E/2$.
Using the proportionality $E \propto T$, we have $\frac{E_2}{E_1} = \frac{T_2}{T_1}$.
Substituting $E_2 = E/2$ and $E_1 = E$ yields $\frac{E/2}{E} = \frac{T_2}{672 \mathrm{K}}$, so $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{T_2}{672 \mathrm{K}}$.

Solving, $T_2 = \frac{672 \mathrm{K}}{2} = 336 \mathrm{K}$.
Converting to Celsius: $T_2 = 336 - 273 = 63^{}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

A van is moving with a speed of $108 \mathrm{ km} / \mathrm{hr}$ on a level road where the coefficient of friction between the tyres and the road is 0.5. For the safe driving of the van, the minimum radius of curvature of the road shall be

For a quantity $Z = X^a Y^b$, the maximum percentage error is given by:

Given $\frac{\Delta F}{F} \times 100\% = 4\%$ and $\frac{\Delta L}{L} \times 100\% = 2\%$, substitution yields:

$\frac{\Delta P}{P} \times 100\% = 4\% + 2 \cdot 2\% = 4\% + 4\% = 8\%$

68951.text:
The angle of minimum deviation produced by a thin prism in air is $\delta_1$. What will be the minimum deviation ($\delta_2$) if the prism is immersed in liquid ?
$\left[ {}^a n_g = \dfrac{3}{2}, \ {}^a n_\ell = \dfrac{1}{3} \right]$
68951.sol:
For a thin prism, the angle of minimum deviation is given by $\delta = (n_{rel} - 1)A$, where $n_{rel}$ is the refractive index of the prism relative to the surrounding medium and $A$ is the angle of the prism.

When the prism is in air, the deviation $\delta_1$ is:
$\delta_1 = ({}^a n_g - 1)A$
Substituting ${}^a n_g = \dfrac{3}{2}$:
$\delta_1 = \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - 1\right)A = \dfrac{A}{2}$

When the prism is immersed in the liquid, the relative refractive index of the glass with respect to the liquid is:
${}^\ell n_g = \dfrac{{}^a n_g}{{}^a n_\ell} = \dfrac{\dfrac{3}{2}}{\dfrac{1}{3}} = \dfrac{9}{2}$

The new deviation $\delta_2$ in the liquid is:
$\delta_2 = ({}^\ell n_g - 1)A$
$\delta_2 = \left(\dfrac{9}{2} - 1\right)A = \dfrac{7A}{2}$

Taking the ratio of $\delta_2$ to $\delta_1$:
$\dfrac{\delta_2}{\delta_1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{7A}{2}}{\dfrac{A}{2}} = 7$

$\delta_2 = 7\delta_1$

Answer: $\delta_2 = 7\,\delta_1$

71071.subject: Biology
71071.text: The available biomass after respiration of producers and other plant losses is __________.
71071.sol:
Gross primary productivity (GPP) of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis.

A considerable amount of GPP is utilised by plants in respiration. Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (R), is the net primary productivity (NPP).

$NPP = GPP - R$

Net primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers).

Answer: Net primary productivity

71206.subject: Biology
71206.text:
Given below are two statements about embryonic development in human.
Statement (I): There is no growth phase between cleavages and the size of blastomeres is reduced.
Statement (II): As the size is reduced, the subsequent cleavages are faster than earlier ones.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
71206.sol:
Statement (I) is correct: Cleavage refers to the series of rapid mitotic divisions that a zygote undergoes. During these divisions, the interphase is very short and lacks the growth phases (G_1$ and $G_2$). Because there is no growth phase between the divisions, the total volume of the embryo remains constant, and the large zygote is partitioned into increasingly smaller cells called blastomeres.

Statement (II) is incorrect: The rate of cleavage does not continuously increase as the size of the blastomeres reduces. In human embryonic development, the first cleavage is relatively long (taking about 30 hours), the next few take about 12 to 24 hours, and as development proceeds towards the blastocyst stage, the cell cycle eventually lengthens. The introduction of $G_1$ and $G_2$ phases (around the mid-blastula transition) causes the subsequent divisions to slow down rather than become faster. Therefore, it is incorrect to state that subsequent cleavages are faster than earlier ones due to size reduction.

Therefore, Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

Answer: Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.$

71480.subject: Biology
71480.text:
Given below are two statements.
Statement I - Inner sporogenous cell is formed from archesporial cell by mitotic division.
Statement II - Outer parietal cell formed from archesporial cell undergoes mitotic divisions to form anther wall layers.
In the light of above statements, select the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both, statement - I and statement - II are correct.
Both, statement - I and statement - II are incorrect.
statement - I is correct but statement - II is incorrect.
statement - I is incorrect but statement - II is correct.
71480.sol:
In the development of an anther, the archesporial cell divides periclinally by mitotic division to form an outer primary parietal cell and an inner primary sporogenous cell. Thus, Statement I is correct.

The outer primary parietal cell undergoes successive periclinal and anticlinal mitotic divisions to form the multiple layers of the anther wall, which include the endothecium, middle layers, and tapetum. Thus, Statement II is also correct.

Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

Answer: Both, statement - I and statement - II are correct.

71557.text: All the following are examples of vertical transport of food through phloem EXCEPT:
options: It occurs from leaves to growing point of stem
It occurs from leaves to developing flowers
It occurs from leaves to fruits
It occurs from phloem to pith.
71557.sol:
Vertical transport of food through phloem involves the movement of synthesized food from the source (leaves) to various sinks located above or below along the plant axis, such as growing points of the stem, developing flowers, and fruits.

Transport of food from the phloem to the pith or cortex occurs laterally across the stem. This is an example of radial or horizontal transport, not vertical transport.

Answer: It occurs from phloem to pith.

71614.subject: Chemistry
71614.text: Phenols react with neutral ferric chloride, then which coloration is NOT produced?
71614.sol:
Phenols react with neutral ferric chloride to form water-soluble coordination complexes. The color of the complex depends on the structure of the specific phenol.

Common colors observed during this test are violet, blue, green, purple, and red. For example, phenol gives a violet color, cresols give a blue color, and catechol gives a green color.

Black coloration is not produced by phenols upon reaction with neutral ferric chloride.

Answer: Black

71890.subject: Chemistry
71890.text: Calculate the pH of the resulting solution obtained by mixing $60\ \text{mL}0.1\ \text{M}$ HCl and $40\ \text{mL}0.1\ \text{M}$ NaOH.
71890.sol:
Millimoles of $\text{HCl} = 60 \times 0.1 = 6\ \text{mmol}$

Millimoles of $\text{NaOH} = 40 \times 0.1 = 4\ \text{mmol}$

Since $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{NaOH}$ react in a $1:1$ ratio, the remaining millimoles of $\text{HCl} = 6 - 4 = 2\ \text{mmol}$.

Total volume of the mixture $= 60 + 40 = 100\ \text{mL}$.

Concentration of $\textH^{+}$ ions in the resulting solution is given by:

$[\textH^{+}] = \dfrac{2\ \text{mmol}}{100\ \text{mL}} = 0.02\ \text{M}$

$\text{pH} = -\log[\textH^{+}] = -\log(2 \times 10^{-2})$

$\text{pH} = 2 - \log 2 = 2 - 0.301 = 1.699$

Answer: $1.699$

72372.subject: Physics
72372.text: For a common emitter amplifier, the audio signal voltage across the collector resistance of $2\ \text{k}\Omega$ is 4 V. If the current amplification factor of the transistor is 100 and the base resistance is $1\ \text{k}\Omega$, then the input voltage is
72372.sol:
Output voltage $V_o = 4\ \text{V}$

Collector resistance $R_c = 2\ \text{k}\Omega = 2000\ \Omega$

Collector current $I_c = \dfrac{V_o}{R_c} = \dfrac{4}{2000} = 2 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{A}$

Current amplification factor $\beta = 100$

Base current $I_b = \dfrac{I_c}{\beta} = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-3}}{100} = 2 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{A}$

Base resistance $R_b = 1\ \text{k}\Omega = 1000\ \Omega$

Input voltage $V_i = I_b R_b = (2 \times 10^{-5}) \times 1000 = 2 \times 10^{-2}\ \text{V} = 20\ \text{mV}$

Answer: $20\ \text{mV}$

75125.text: Which of the following main industry/industries was/were developed in the second industrial revolution that took place after about 1850?
75125.sol:
The first industrial revolution, which began in the late 18th century, was primarily based on coal, iron, steam engines, and the mechanization of the textile industry (cotton spinning and weaving).

The second industrial revolution, which took place after about 1850, was characterized by rapid industrialization and the development of new industries such as steel, chemicals, electricity, and petroleum.

Therefore, the chemical and electrical industries were the main industries developed during the second industrial revolution.

Answer: Chemical and electrical

75201.text:
Which of the following statements with reference to shadow zones in an event of an earthquake is/are correct?
1. Zone between 105° and 145° from epicentre was identified as the shadow zone for both P-waves and S-waves
2. The shadow zone of P-waves is much larger than that of the S-waves
Select the answer using the code given below:
75201.sol:
Seismographs located at any distance within $105^{{}^{\circ}}$ from the epicentre record the arrival of both P-waves and S-waves. However, seismographs located beyond $145^{{}^{\circ}}$ from the epicentre record the arrival of P-waves, but not S-waves.

Thus, the zone between $105^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $145^{{}^{\circ}}$ from the epicentre is identified as the shadow zone for both types of waves. Hence, statement 1 is correct.

The entire zone beyond $105^{{}^{\circ}}$ does not receive S-waves. The shadow zone of S-waves is much larger than that of P-waves, covering over $40\%$ of the earth's surface. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.

Answer: 1 only

79343.sol:
The activity of cambium is under the control of many physiological and environmental factors. Such activity can be observed in the form of annual rings.

In temperate regions, the climatic conditions are not uniform through the year.

  • In the spring, cambium is very active and produces a large number of xylary elements having vessels with wider cavities. The wood formed is called early wood or spring wood.
  • In winter, the cambium is less active and forms fewer xylary elements that have narrow vessels. The wood formed is called late wood or autumn wood.

79465.text:
Consider following features:

  • Organ system level of organisation
  • Bilateral symmetry
  • True coelomates with segmentation of body.

Select the correct option of animal group which possess all the above characteristics:
79465.sol:
Organ system level organization, bilateral symmetry, true coelomates with the segmentation of body are seen in Annelida, Arthropoda, and Chordata.

Annelids possess metameric segmentation.

Arthropods have segmented bodies, like the annelids. These segments have become specialized, however, with one pair of jointed appendages added to each segment. Among living arthropods, the millipedes most closely suggest what the ancestral arthropod might have looked like.

Chordates use heteromeric segmentation in which the link between segmented parts appears more subtly.

86507.subject: Mathematics
86507.text: In a building, an elevator starts from the ground floor (that is, 0th floor) with $10$ passengers and stops at every floor until the 15th floor which is the topmost floor. No new passengers enter the elevator on any floor from the 1st through the 15th floor. If all the passengers got off the elevator then the probability that at most one passenger got off at each floor is
86507.sol:
Total number of passengers is $10$.

Total number of floors where passengers can get off is $15$ (from the 1st to the 15th floor).

Since each passenger can get off at any of the $15$ floors, the total number of ways for the $10$ passengers to get off is $15^{10}$.

The condition that at most one passenger gets off at each floor implies that all $10$ passengers must get off at $10$ distinct floors.

The number of ways to choose $10$ floors out of $15$ is ^{15}C_{10}$.

The number of ways the 10$ passengers can be arranged in these $10$ chosen floors is $10!$.

The number of favorable ways is ^{15}C_{10} \times 10! = $\dfrac{15!}{10!5!} \times 10! = \dfrac{15!}{5!} .

The required probability is the ratio of the number of favorable ways to the total number of ways, which is \dfrac{15!}{5! \times 15^{10}}$.

95198.subject: Botany
options: In flowering plants, tracheids and vessels are the main water transporting elements.
In gymnosperms, tracheids are the chief water transporting elements
The companion cells play an important role in the maintenance of a pressure gradient in the sieve tubes
95198.sol:
Gymnosperms lack vessels in their xylem. Tracheids are elongated or tube-like cells with thick and lignified walls and tapering ends. These are dead and are without protoplasm. The inner layers of the cell walls have thickenings which vary in form. In flowering plants, tracheids and vessels are the main water transporting elements. The vessel is a long cylindrical tube-like structure made up of many cells called vessel members, each with lignified walls and a large central cavity.

Companion cells, along with phloem parenchyma play an important role in the maintenance of a pressure gradient in the sieve tubes.

100119.subject: Physics
100119.text: Which of the following physical quantities has the SI unit $\text{kg m s}^{-3} \text{K}^{-1}$?
100119.sol:
Let us express the given unit in terms of familiar derived SI units:

Given unit: $\text{kg m s}^{-3} \text{K}^{-1}$

We know that the unit of energy (Joule, $\text{J}$) is $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$.
Multiplying and dividing the given unit by $\text{m}$, we can group the terms as follows:

$(\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}) \text{s}^{-1} \text{m}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}$

Substituting $\text{J}$ for $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$:

$\text{J s}^{-1} \text{m}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}$

Since the rate of energy transfer ($\text{J s}^{-1}$) is Watt ($\text{W}$), the unit simplifies to:

$\text{W m}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}$

This is the standard SI unit for thermal conductivity, which can be verified from the heat conduction equation $H = \dfrac{K A \Delta T}{l}$.

Answer: Thermal conductivity

100800.text:
Consider the following statements $A$ and $B$ identify the correct answer given below :
(A) A body initially at rest is acted upon by a constant force. The rate of change of its kinetic energy varies linearly with time
(B) When a body is at rest, it must be in equilibrium.
100800.sol:
$\mathrm{KE}=\frac{1}{2} m v^2=\frac{1}{2} m(a t)^2=\frac{1}{2} m a^2 t^2$
Rate of change of KE,
$\frac{d K}{d t}=\frac{d}{d t}\left(\frac{1}{2} m a^2 t^2\right)=m a^2 t$
$\therefore \quad \frac{d K}{d t} \propto t$
So, statement $A$ is correct.
When the body is at rest, then it may be or may not be in equilibrium, so statement $B$ is wrong.

101201.subject: Physics
101201.text: A uniform solid cylinder of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rolling without slipping on a flat horizontal surface. Its centre of mass moves with a constant speed $v$. If $L_C$ is the magnitude of its angular momentum about its centre of mass and $L_P$ is the magnitude of its angular momentum about a stationary point $P$ on the ground, the ratio $\dfrac{L_C}{L_P}$ is:
101201.sol:
For a solid cylinder rolling without slipping, the angular velocity is $\omega = \dfrac{v}{R}$.

The angular momentum about the centre of mass is given by:
$L_C = I_{cm}\omega = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}MR^2\right)\left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}MvR$

The angular momentum about a stationary point $P$ on the ground is the sum of the angular momentum about the centre of mass and the angular momentum of the centre of mass about $P$:
$\vec{L}_P = \vec{L}_C + \vec{r}_{cm} \times M\vec{v}_{cm}$

Since the cylinder is rolling on the ground, the perpendicular distance from $P$ to the line of motion of the centre of mass is $R$. Both the spin and orbital angular momentum vectors point in the same direction.

Thus, the magnitude is:
$L_P = L_C + MvR = \dfrac{1}{2}MvR + MvR = \dfrac{3}{2}MvR$

The required ratio is:
$\dfrac{L_C}{L_P} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}MvR}{\dfrac{3}{2}MvR} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{3}$

101786.text: The neck and bottom of a bottle are 3 cm and 15 cm in radius respectively. If the cork is pressed with a force 12 N in the neck of the bottle, then force exerted on the bottom of the bottle is

Pressure at neck of bottle
$p_1=\frac{F_1}{A_1}=\frac{F_1}{\pi r_1^2}$
Similarly, pressure at bottom of bottle
$p_2=\frac{F_2}{A_2}=\frac{F_2}{\pi r_2^2}$
According to Pascal's law, liquids transmit pressure equal in all directions.
$\therefore \begin{aligned}
\frac{F_1}{\pi r_1^2} & =\frac{F_2}{\pi r_2^2} \\
\frac{12}{\pi(3)^2} & =\frac{F_2}{\pi(15)^2} \\
F_2 & =\frac{12 \times 15 \times 15}{3 \times 3} \\
F_2 & =300 \mathrm{~N}
\end{aligned}$

103144.subject: Physics
103144.text: Five capacitors are connected to form a Wheatstone bridge network between terminals $A$ and $B$. The first branch between $A$ and $B$ consists of two capacitors in series having capacitances $C$ and $3C$. The second branch between $A$ and $B$ consists of two capacitors in series having capacitances $5 \mu\text{F}$ and $15 \mu\text{F}$. A central capacitor of $10 \mu\text{F}$ connects the junction of the first branch to the junction of the second branch. If the potential difference across the $10 \mu\text{F}$ capacitor is zero and the equivalent capacitance of the network between $A$ and $B$ is $6 \mu\text{F}$, the value of $C$ is :
103144.sol:
Since the potential difference across the $10 \mu\text{F}$ capacitor is zero, the bridge is balanced and the central capacitor can be removed from the circuit.

The equivalent capacitance of the upper branch (series combination of $C$ and $3C$) is:
$C_{\text{upper}} = \dfrac{C \times 3C}{C + 3C} = \dfrac{3C}{4}$

The equivalent capacitance of the lower branch (series combination of $5 \mu\text{F}$ and $15 \mu\text{F}$) is:
$C_{\text{lower}} = \dfrac{5 \times 15}{5 + 15} = \dfrac{75}{20} = \dfrac{15}{4} \mu\text{F}$

The total equivalent capacitance is the parallel combination of the upper and lower branches:
$C_{\text{eq}} = C_{\text{upper}} + C_{\text{lower}}$
$6 = \dfrac{3C}{4} + \dfrac{15}{4}$
$24 = 3C + 15$
$3C = 9 \Rightarrow C = 3 \mu\text{F}$

Answer: $3 \mu\text{F}$

104610.text: The frequency of a light wave in a material is $2 \times 10^{14} \mathrm{~Hz}$ and wavelength is $5000 Å$. The refractive index of material will be
104610.sol:
Velocity of light waves in material is
$v=\mathrm{v} \lambda\ldots(i)$
Refractive index of material is
$\mu=\frac{c}{v}\ldots(ii)$
where $c$ is speed of light in vacuum or air.
or

Hence, from Eq. (iii), we get
$\mu=\frac{3 \times 10^8}{2 \times 10^{14} \times 5000 \times 10^{-10}}=3.00$

104684.subject: Physics
104684.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When unpolarised light is incident on a transparent surface at Brewster's angle, the reflected ray and the refracted ray are mutually perpendicular.
Reason (R): At Brewster's angle, the electric field vectors of the completely polarised reflected light vibrate parallel to the plane of incidence.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
104684.sol:
According to Brewster's law, when unpolarised light is incident at the polarising angle (Brewster's angle), the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other. Thus, Assertion (A) is correct.

The reflected light is completely plane-polarised, and its electric field vectors vibrate perpendicular to the plane of incidence, not parallel to it. Thus, Reason (R) is incorrect.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

104728.subject: Physics
104728.text:
Consider the following four optical arrangements intended to produce an interference pattern on a screen:
(I) Two independent sodium lamps of the same wattage placed close to each other.
(II) Two narrow slits illuminated by a single monochromatic laser beam.
(III) Two independent laser pointers emitting light of the exact same wavelength.
(IV) Light from a single narrow slit and its reflection from a plane mirror.

How many of the above arrangements will successfully produce a sustained interference pattern?
104728.sol:
For a sustained interference pattern to be observed, the sources of light must be coherent, meaning they must maintain a constant phase difference with respect to time.

(I) Two independent sodium lamps are incoherent sources because light is emitted by independent atoms randomly, leading to a rapidly changing phase difference. They will not produce a sustained pattern.

(II) Two narrow slits illuminated by a single laser beam act as coherent sources because they are derived from the same original wavefront (Young's double-slit setup). They will produce a sustained pattern.

(III) Two independent laser pointers, despite being highly monochromatic, are still independent sources. Their relative phase will drift randomly, so they cannot produce a sustained interference pattern.

(IV) Light from a single slit and its reflection from a plane mirror act as two coherent sources because the reflected virtual source is derived from the real source (Lloyd's mirror setup). They will produce a sustained pattern.

Thus, only two arrangements (II and IV) will produce a sustained interference pattern.

Answer: Only two

105908.subject: Chemistry
105908.text:
A sample of ethane ($C_2H_6$) is subjected to complete combustion, producing exactly $88$ g of carbon dioxide. The mass of ethane combusted in this process is
(Given: atomic mass in amu H $=1$, C $=12$ and O $=16$)
105908.sol:
The balanced chemical equation for the complete combustion of ethane is:

$C_2H_6 + \dfrac{7}{2}O_2 \rightarrow 2CO_2 + 3H_2O$

Molar mass of $CO_2 = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44$ g/mol

Number of moles of $CO_2$ produced $= \dfrac{88}{44} = 2$ moles

From the balanced equation, $1$ mole of ethane ($C_2H_6$) produces $2$ moles of $CO_2$.

Therefore, exactly $1$ mole of ethane must have been combusted to produce $2$ moles of $CO_2$.

Molar mass of ethane ($C_2H_6$) $= 2 \times 12 + 6 \times 1 = 30$ g/mol

Mass of ethane combusted $= 1 \times 30 = 30$ g

Answer: $30$ g

107016.text:
Three unknown oxides A, B, and C exhibit the following chemical behaviour:
Oxide A does not show acidic or basic properties.
Oxide B reacts with aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ as well as with $\mathrm{HCl}$.
Oxide C reacts with water to form a strongly acidic solution.

The correct combination of formulas for oxides A, B, and C respectively is:
107016.sol:
Oxide A does not show acidic or basic properties, meaning it is a neutral oxide. Examples of neutral oxides include $\mathrm{N_2O}$, $\mathrm{NO}$, and $\mathrm{CO}$.

Oxide B reacts with both a strong base ($\mathrm{NaOH}$) and a strong acid ($\mathrm{HCl}$), which indicates it is an amphoteric oxide. Examples include $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ and $\mathrm{ZnO}$.

Oxide C reacts with water to form a strongly acidic solution, meaning it is an acidic oxide. Examples include $\mathrm{SO_3}$ (forms $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$) and $\mathrm{P_4O_{10}}$ (forms $\mathrm{H_3PO_4}$).

Evaluating the options:
Option 1: $\mathrm{N_2O}$ is neutral, $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ is amphoteric, and $\mathrm{SO_3}$ is acidic. This matches the required profile exactly.
Option 2 is incorrect because $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is acidic and $\mathrm{Na_2O}$ is basic.
Option 3 is incorrect because $\mathrm{MgO}$ is basic, not amphoteric.
Option 4 is incorrect because $\mathrm{BaO}$ is basic, not amphoteric.

Answer: $\mathrm{N_2O}$, $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$, $\mathrm{SO_3}$

According to VSEPR theory:

$\mathrm{XeF}_4$ has 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs on the central Xe atom. Its geometry is square planar. The lone pairs are opposite to each other, and the four Xe-F bond dipoles cancel each other out, resulting in a net dipole moment $\mu = 0$.

$\mathrm{SF}_4$ has 4 bond pairs and 1 lone pair on the central S atom. Its geometry is see-saw. Due to its asymmetrical shape, the bond dipoles do not cancel out, resulting in $\mu \neq 0$.

$\mathrm{PCl}_5$ has 5 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs on the central P atom. Its geometry is trigonal bipyramidal. The three equatorial P-Cl bond dipoles cancel each other, and the two axial P-Cl bond dipoles cancel each other, resulting in a perfectly symmetrical molecule with $\mu = 0$.

$\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ has 2 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs on the central O atom. Its geometry is bent. The bond dipoles and lone pair dipoles do not cancel out, resulting in $\mu \neq 0$.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(i), (B)-(ii), (C)-(iii), (D)-(iv).

Answer: (A)-(i), (B)-(ii), (C)-(iii), (D)-(iv)

108636.subject: Chemistry
108636.text:
An ideal gas expands isothermally at temperature $T$ from volume $V_1$ to $V_2$ via two different paths:
Path I: Reversible isothermal expansion
Path II: Isothermal free expansion (against vacuum)

Consider the following statements regarding these two paths:
(a) The change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) of the gas is zero for both paths.
(b) The change in entropy of the system ($\Delta S_{\text{system}}$) is the same for both paths.
(c) The change in entropy of the surroundings ($\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}}$) is the same for both paths.
(d) The work done by the gas is the same for both paths.

How many of the above statements are correct?
108636.sol:
For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process, the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) depends only on temperature. Since temperature is constant for both paths, $\Delta U = 0$ for both. Thus, statement (a) is correct.

Entropy is a state function. Since both paths operate between the same initial and final states, the change in entropy of the system ($\Delta S_{\text{system}}$) is identical for both paths. Thus, statement (b) is correct.

The change in entropy of the surroundings ($\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}}$) depends on the actual heat exchanged. For Path I (reversible), heat is absorbed from the surroundings, so $\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} = -nR \ln(V_2/V_1)$. For Path II (free expansion), the external pressure is zero, so work done $W = 0$. Since $\Delta U = 0$, the heat exchanged $q = 0$, making $\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} = 0$. Thus, statement (c) is incorrect.

Work is a path function. For Path I, $W = -nRT \ln(V_2/V_1)$. For Path II, $W = 0$. Thus, statement (d) is incorrect.

Exactly two statements, (a) and (b), are correct.

Answer: Two

108956.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For the synthesis of ammonia ($\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$), the numerical value of $K_p$ is smaller than $K_c$ at $298\text{ K}$.

Reason (R): $K_p$ and $K_c$ are related by the expression $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}$, where $\Delta n$ is the difference between the total number of moles of all products and all reactants.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
108956.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: For the reaction $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$, the change in gaseous moles is $\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$.
The relation is $K_p = K_c(RT)^{-2} = \dfrac{K_c}{(RT)^2}$.
At $298\text{ K}$, the value of $RT$ is approximately $0.0831 \times 298 \approx 24.76 \text{ L bar K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$, which is significantly greater than $1$. Thus, $(RT)^2 > 1$, making $K_p < K_c$.

Reason (R) is incorrect: The term $\Delta n$ (or $\Delta n_g$) in the relation $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$ specifically represents the difference between the number of moles of gaseous products and gaseous reactants, not all products and all reactants. Solids and liquids must be excluded from this calculation.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

114240.subject: Chemistry
114240.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I : In electrochemical cells, Gibbs energy of spontaneous redox reaction is converted into electrical work.
Statement-II : Gibb's energy can be calculated by using \(\Delta \mathrm{G}=-\mathrm{nFE}\) & it is an intensive property. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and II are incorrect.
Both statement I and II are correct.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
114240.sol:
Statement-I:
In electrochemical cells, spontaneous redox reactions generate an electric potential difference. The Gibbs energy (\($\Delta \mathrm{G}$\)) of the reaction is converted into electrical work, which is measured as the electromotive force (EMF) of the cell. This is a fundamental principle of electrochemistry.
Statement-II:
The Gibbs energy (\($\Delta \mathrm{G}$\)) can indeed be calculated using the equation:
\($\Delta \mathrm{G}=-\mathrm{nFE}$\)
where:
n = number of electrons transferred
F = Faraday constant (\(96485 $\mathrm{C}$/ $\mathrm{mol}$\))
E = cell potential (in volts)
Gibbs energy is an extensive property, but \($\Delta \mathrm{G}$\) (change in Gibbs energy) is an intensive property, as it is independent of the system size.
Since both statements are correct, the answer is option (2).
Intensive properties are independent of the system size or amount of substance, unlike extensive properties which depend on the amount of substance. Examples of intensive properties include temperature, pressure, and concentration.

120984.text: Identify the correct statement regarding the cofactor present in the enzyme peroxidase.
options: It is haem, which acts as a co-enzyme and binds transiently to the apoenzyme.
It is haem, which is a prosthetic group and is tightly bound to the apoenzyme.
It is zinc, which forms coordination bonds with side chains at the active site.
It is haem, which is an inorganic metal ion that binds tightly to the apoenzyme.
120984.sol:
In the enzymes peroxidase and catalase, which catalyse the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen, haem is the cofactor.

Haem is a prosthetic group. According to NCERT, prosthetic groups are organic compounds that are distinguished from other cofactors in that they are tightly bound to the apoenzyme.

Zinc is a metal ion cofactor for carboxypeptidase, not peroxidase. Co-enzymes associate only transiently, whereas haem in peroxidase is tightly bound. Haem is an organic compound (porphyrin derivative), not an inorganic metal ion.

Answer: It is haem, which is a prosthetic group and is tightly bound to the apoenzyme.

122218.sol: They may be aquatic (marine and fresh water) or terrestrial; free-living, and sometimes parasitic. They exhibit organ-system level of body organisation and bilateral symmetry. 123001.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The ovary of Brinjal and Tobacco is bicarpellary and syncarpous with a swollen placenta.
Reason (R): They belong to the family Solanaceae, which is characterized by parietal placentation and the formation of a false septum.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
123001.sol:
Assertion (A) is true. Brinjal and Tobacco belong to the family Solanaceae. The characteristic features of the gynoecium in Solanaceae include a bicarpellary, syncarpous, superior ovary that is bilocular with a swollen placenta and many ovules.

Reason (R) is false. Members of the family Solanaceae exhibit axile placentation, not parietal placentation. Parietal placentation and the formation of a false septum (replum) are characteristic features of the family Brassicaceae (e.g., Mustard).

Therefore, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
